+"""Safe retrieval of plugin attributes for diagnostic display."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from typing import Any
+
+from _pytest.outcomes import TEST_OUTCOME
+
+
+__all__ = ["plugin_metadata"]
+
+
+def plugin_metadata(
+    plugin: object, names: Iterable[str], default: Any = None
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return a dictionary mapping each of ``names`` to the corresponding
+    attribute of ``plugin``.
+
+    Intended for diagnostic display, so it never fails because of a
+    misbehaving plugin: if an attribute is missing, or accessing it raises an
+    :class:`Exception` or a pytest outcome exception (such as ``skip()``),
+    ``default`` is used instead. Falsey attribute values are kept as-is.
+    Other :class:`BaseException` subclasses (e.g. :class:`KeyboardInterrupt`,
+    :class:`SystemExit`) propagate.
+    """
+    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for name in names:
+        try:
+            value = getattr(plugin, name)
+        except TEST_OUTCOME:
+            value = default
+        result[name] = value
+    return result

+++ b/testing/test_plugin_metadata.py
@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from _pytest.plugin_metadata import plugin_metadata
+import pytest
+
+
+class Plugin:
+    version = "1.0"
+    count = 0
+    enabled = False
+    name = ""
+    items: list[Any] = []
+    nothing = None
+
+    @property
+    def broken(self) -> str:
+        raise RuntimeError("boom")
+
+    @property
+    def skipping(self) -> str:
+        pytest.skip("not available")
+
+    @property
+    def failing(self) -> str:
+        pytest.fail("not available")
+
+    @property
+    def interrupted(self) -> str:
+        raise KeyboardInterrupt
+
+    @property
+    def exiting(self) -> str:
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+
+def test_no_names() -> None:
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), []) == {}
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), (), default="x") == {}
+
+
+def test_present_attributes() -> None:
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), ["version"]) == {"version": "1.0"}
+
+
+def test_falsey_values_kept() -> None:
+    names = ["count", "enabled", "name", "items", "nothing"]
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), names, default="missing") == {
+        "count": 0,
+        "enabled": False,
+        "name": "",
+        "items": [],
+        "nothing": None,
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["missing", "broken", "skipping", "failing"])
+def test_default_used(name: str) -> None:
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), [name]) == {name: None}
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), [name], default="?") == {name: "?"}
+
+
+def test_module_plugin() -> None:
+    import types
+
+    mod = types.ModuleType("someplugin")
+    mod.__version__ = "2.0"  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    assert plugin_metadata(mod, ["__version__", "__author__"]) == {
+        "__version__": "2.0",
+        "__author__": None,
+    }
+
+
+def test_generator_names() -> None:
+    names = (n for n in ["version", "missing"])
+    assert plugin_metadata(Plugin(), names, default=0) == {
+        "version": "1.0",
+        "missing": 0,
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("name", "exc"),
+    [("interrupted", KeyboardInterrupt), ("exiting", SystemExit)],
+)
+def test_base_exceptions_propagate(name: str, exc: type[BaseException]) -> None:
+    with pytest.raises(exc):
+        plugin_metadata(Plugin(), ["version", name])
